Aliens 4K is a bit of an abomination. James Cameron has gone overboard with digital processing on his 4K releases and the results look less like film and more like fake and rubberish AI. Better sticking with the regular blu-ray if you already have it.

[mingofmongo] unless you're torrenting a 50gb file, you're getting a compressed version of what's on the disc. Discs include uncompressed Atmos soundtracks, and generally guarantee some form of HDR. These things are unreliably available on Torrents. Uncompressed Atmos isn't available at all on streaming services.
[Jake T] Quality mostly. No stream can match the bitrate of a disk. And we’re talking 60-100GB per movie if you want the same quality from a torrent.
I get why most people would choose streaming, but I love owning the things that make me happy :-)

[thegreatermamba] Sorry for the noob question - why people still are interested in buying Discs when these can be purchased in high quality via Apple TV Store or Prime? Physical discs require BluRay players and your library is not available everywhere as compared to Digital purchases.
[Mjk698] Nostalgia mostly but actually owning something and not being held hostage by the big corporate
[S Baldrick] With most digital stores, you don't own the media.
Exhibit A
[Deditus] The quality isn't the same, and you don't really own digital goods. There's been plenty of cases where the media you paid for suddenly isn't available anymore. If you have it physically you have some measure of control over it.
[stevtom27] Quality on disc is usually better than streaming. Its usually a higher bitrate even if the streaming service offers a 2160p 4k option. Plus you dont need to pay multiple subscriptions to different companies to find the movie you want.
[CheapOjoe] The main reason is quality. Under the right conditions a large OLED TV in a dimly lit room with a good surround sound system a 4K Blu-ray disc can look noticeably better and sound significantly better than even the highest quality digital purchase because it uses much less compression.
That said, for watching on a phone, tablet, laptop, or even casual viewing on a TV, most people probably won't notice much, if any, difference. Digital purchases are far more convenient since your library is available almost anywhere without needing a Blu-ray player.
So it really comes down to priorities: if you value the absolute best picture and audio quality, physical discs are still the gold standard. If you value convenience, digital is hard to beat.
As others have mentioned, there's also true ownership you don't need a subscription, monthly fees, or an internet connection to watch your movies.
